brief: The Fed raised rates 25 bps to 3.75%-4.00% in a unanimous 12-0 vote, its first hike since 2023. Chair Warsh's hawkish press conference, citing a resilient economy and persistent inflation, triggered a broader repricing: the 2-year Treasury yield rose to a two-year high of 4.73%, the 10-year climbed back above 5%, oil fell nearly 3%, the S&P 500 fell 0.4% and the dollar gained 0.6%. The dot plot signals one more hike by year-end then a pause through 2027, which Raymond James reads as a mid-cycle adjustment, not a prolonged tightening cycle, that should not alter growth or earnings. SPR drawdowns have slowed to their weakest pace since March as reserves near minimum safety levels. US output has rebounded to a record-matching ~14m bpd, but that offsets only ~5% of the Persian Gulf supply loss, leaving demand destruction needed until the Strait of Hormuz reopens. August retail sales beat at 1.2% MoM, with the 1.4% control-group gain pointing to a 3Q GDP boost, though RJ expects growth to moderate. The S&P 500 Equal Weight Index and 10-year yield show their most negative correlation since 1996, as rising yields are now read as a financing headwind rather than a growth signal.
